status: DRAFT — pending Agni Gate 1 review before run
motivation: The Lyra Technique II paper claims a monotonic persona-intensity gradient (L0<L0.5<L1<L2<L3 in geometric separability) but ships only L0-vs-L3 and one L0-vs-L0.5 scalar. The per-level breakdown asserted in section 5.2 has no backing data. This experiment produces all adjacent-level pairwise AUROCs to test the gradient directly.
primary_hypothesis: Geometric separability between persona levels increases monotonically with level separation: Spearman rho(level-gap, AUROC) > 0, p < 0.05.
secondary_predictions: AUROC(L0 vs L3) is the largest pairwise value.
Each adjacent-level AUROC (L0-L0.5, L0.5-L1, L1-L2, L2-L3) exceeds 0.5 but is individually weaker than the L0-L3 endpoint.
The NULL control (L0 vs L0, prompts split in half) is ~0.5, confirming no spurious separability.

design.held_constant: user prompt content (24 neutral explanatory prompts, identical across all levels)
design.features: per-layer SVD stable_rank + spectral_entropy at L3/L7/L11/L15, plus W_K emotion projections
design.rationale: Holding prompt content constant means any geometric difference is attributable to persona intensity, not content. This is the control the original experiment lacked.

red_team_controls.C1: prompt content identical across levels (only system prompt varies)
red_team_controls.C2: FWL residualization on prompt_len within each CV fold
red_team_controls.C3: GroupKFold on prompt_idx (no prompt in both train and test)
red_team_controls.C5: bootstrap CIs (2000 resamples) on every AUROC
red_team_controls.C8: monotonicity tested via Spearman, not visual inspection

falsification_conditions: If the NULL control (L0 vs L0) AUROC > 0.65, the pipeline has a leakage bug — STOP, do not interpret.
If monotonicity Spearman is non-significant (p > 0.05), the gradient claim is FALSIFIED and the paper must drop 'monotonic'.
If adjacent AUROCs are non-monotonic (e.g., L1-L2 > L2-L3), report the actual ordering, not the claimed one.
decision_rule: Report the actual pairwise AUROC matrix regardless of outcome. If the gradient is confirmed, it backs the section 5.2 claim. If not, section 5.2 is corrected to match the data. Either way the paper gains the per-level data it currently lacks.
run_protocol: 1. Agni Gate 1 design review (red team the design).
2. python3 persona_per_level.py --pilot  (6 prompts, verify pipeline + null control)
3. Inspect pilot: confirm NULL ~0.5 and features extract cleanly.
5. Agni Gate 3 result review before committing to paper.
